original_shows: A Wardrobe/Vanity UI where the player customizes their large-headed 2D cartoon avatar by clicking on various masks, hats, and outfits (such as the Imperial Caterpillar Mask, Sloth Mask, Chicken Mask, Top Hat, and Piggycorn Ride), previewing them on the avatar, and clicking Test.
rebuild_shows: A Wardrobe & Store Catalog modal with a large-headed 2D cartoon avatar preview, slots for layered clothing (Hat/Mask, Coat/Cape, Shirt/Top, Pants/Skirt/Dress, Shoes), facial feature toggles (Skin, Hair, Eyes, Nose, Mouth, Ears), and catalog items including Imperial Caterpillar Mask, Red Top Hat, Piggy Ride, etc., which update the avatar preview and in-world character when equipped.
difference: None significant; art is simplified vector style and UI is a modal overlay rather than a full webpage, but all avatar customization features, slots, and items correspond.

original_shows: Avatars are full-body characters with limbs, hands, feet, and distinct animations. When drinking Pumpkin Ale (29:43), the avatar gains a glowing blue aura around its body and performs a zombie-like Thriller dance animation, which later synchronizes with nearby players (29:57).
rebuild_shows: Avatars are simple circle heads on rectangle bodies with no arms or legs. Walking and jumping just move the static sprite. When drinking Pumpkin Ale (00:05), a translucent blue circle appears around the character and they just bob/rotate slightly in place alongside a nearby player, lacking actual limb/dance animations.
difference: The rebuild lacks proper body/limb animations for idle, walking, jumping (arms/hair lifting, legs tucked), and the Thriller zombie-dance animation.
fix_hint: Add articulated limbs/frames to player avatars to animate walking, jumping (tucked legs, lifted arms/hair), idle breathing/blinking, and the Thriller zombie-dance pose.

original_shows: The player avatar jumps up the multi-tiered porch, awning, and roof ledges of the house on Beau's Home Street using arc-based jumps with mid-air horizontal control.
rebuild_shows: The player avatar walks over to the house on Beau's Home Street and jumps up onto the porch roof and then the upper roof tiers.
difference: None in behavior; the multi-tiered roof jumping works as expected.

original_shows: A player avatar (Artichoke) is shrunk to miniature scale while maintaining normal animations and movement alongside normal-sized players.
rebuild_shows: The player consumes items to shrink to miniature size and embiggen to giant size while walking and maintaining normal movement animations.
difference: None.

original_shows: As the player walks left and right across the street, the camera smoothly tracks them horizontally, with the foreground elements, mid-ground dark tree silhouettes, and distant foggy forest background scrolling at different parallax speeds.
rebuild_shows: As the player runs right and left, the camera tracks horizontally within the street bounds, with foreground objects, mid-ground black trees, and distant grey tree layers moving at different parallax rates.
difference: The rebuild uses simplified geometric art for the trees and characters, and moves faster during the automated test, but the camera tracking and multi-layered parallax scrolling behavior match.

original_shows: In the top-right of the game viewport, hovering near the current location label ('Bonto's Home Street') reveals a horizontal mini-map strip showing the street layout, dots for entities/players, and a '< World' button on the left side. Clicking '< World' opens the World Map modal, where clicking a region (Zhambu) opens the region's street network map, and clicking a street node shows options like 'Teleport here', 'Create Link for Chat', and 'Set as Destination'.
rebuild_shows: In the top-right of the game viewport beneath 'Current location: Beau's Home Street', there is a horizontal mini-map strip showing a '< World' button on the left, the street layout, and coloured dots for players/NPCs. Clicking it opens the World Map modal, and clicking a region opens the region street network map with options 'Teleport here', 'Create Link for Chat', and 'Set as destination'.
difference: None significant to the rule under test (the mini-map strip in the rebuild is persistently visible rather than hover-revealed, and the world map art is stylized/diagrammatic, which is acceptable).

original_shows: Clicking the World Map icon opens a World Map showing multiple landmasses/regions (like Zhambu). Clicking a region opens a Region Map showing a network of interconnected streets represented as dashed lines with circular nodes/dots along them; clicking a street node opens a popover with 'Teleport here', 'Create Link for Chat', and 'Set as destination'.
rebuild_shows: Clicking the World Map opens a 'World Map of Ur' dialog with colored ovals for regions (Zhambu, Kalavana, Ixeta, Home Streets, Andra) and a right-hand panel with street buttons and teleport options. It never opens a Region Map showing interconnected streets as dashed lines and nodes.
difference: The rebuild lacks the Region Map view with interconnected streets drawn as dashed lines and clickable nodes; instead it just shows oval blobs for regions and a list of street buttons on the side.
fix_hint: Implement the Region Map view (when clicking a region like Zhambu or Kalavana on the World Map) that renders the region's streets as a graph of dashed line segments and circular nodes, with a popover appearing over the clicked node.
test_problem: The test only opened the top-level World Map and did not click into a region to verify the Region Map's dashed-line street network.

original_shows: Walking past the wooden signpost at the left street boundary triggers a full-canvas loading screen with a wide banner image of the street, overlaid white text ('Entering / Bongul Beat / in Andra', 'Home to: ...'), and a bottom progress bar that says 'loading...' then 'reticulating splines... XX%'.
rebuild_shows: Walking to the left signpost triggers a loading screen with a small square solid-color thumbnail on the left, dark text on a white background to the right ('Entering / Chego Chase in Andra', 'Home to: ...'), and a progress bar that only says 'loading... 22%' (no 'reticulating splines...' shown before transitioning).
difference: 1) The loading screen layout differs significantly: the original has a full-width street preview banner with text overlaid inside the banner, whereas the rebuild has a small square box on the left with text beside it on a white background. 2) The loading bar text in the rebuild only shows 'loading... 22%' and does not show 'reticulating splines...' as required by the rule.
fix_hint: Ensure the loading bar displays 'reticulating splines... XX%' during street transitions, and update the loading card layout so the street preview spans the card width with white text overlaid on it (matching the original Glitch loading screen design).

original_shows: On Chego Chase, hovering/approaching the Ministry of Departments doors highlights the door frame in teal/cyan. Interacting with the doors transitions the player into the interior street 'Andra Bureaucratic Hall' (showing 'Department of Administrative Affairs / Ministry of Departments' on the wall, a desk, water cooler, waiting area chairs, and a first-visit XP notification).
rebuild_shows: On Chego Chase, the Ministry of Departments building has doors that highlight with a teal/cyan border and tooltip ('Enter Andra Bureaucratic Hall'), and clicking them transitions the player into the interior 'Andra Bureaucratic Hall' with corresponding wall text, furniture, and first-visit XP notification.
difference: None relevant to the rule (minor art/loading screen differences only).

original_shows: Upon entering Bongul Beat for the first time, a top-left toast notification and a message in the right-hand Local Chat / Activity feed appear saying 'This is your first visit to Bongul Beat. You received 1xp!'.
rebuild_shows: Upon entering Goli Grabs in Kalavana for the first time, a top-left toast notification and a message in the right-hand Local Chat / Activity feed appear saying 'This is your first visit to Goli Grabs in Kalavana. You received 2 xp!'.
difference: None. Both show the first-visit notification and XP bonus in both the top-left toast and the right-hand activity feed.

original_shows: In the original clip, the player enters Goli Grabs in Kalavana, walks around briefly, and then opens the top-left avatar menu and clicks 'Go home' to teleport back to their Home Street.
rebuild_shows: In the rebuild clip, the player opens the World Map, selects Goli Grabs in Kalavana and clicks 'Teleport here (-10e)', arriving at Goli Grabs. Then the player opens the top-left avatar menu and clicks 'Go home (Beau's Home Street)', returning to Beau's Home Street.
difference: None for the rule under test (both World Map teleportation and the top-left 'Go home' menu functionality are present and working).

original_shows: Clicking Butler Roy (Beau) outside the house on Beau's Home Street opens a popup menu with options ('Muffle butterfly wisdom', 'Stop telling me things visitors say', 'Zip lip', 'Set pace', 'Yoo-hoo', 'Gipe', 'Leave info', 'Animations', 'Mailbox', 'Who visited?'). Selecting 'Who visited?' makes Roy display a speech bubble ('There were a lot of visitors. I'll IM you the list.' with a 'Thanks!' button) and sends a Butler IM in the right sidebar listing recent visitors.
rebuild_shows: Clicking Butler Roy (Beau) outside the house on Beau's Home Street opens the same popup menu with all matching options. Selecting 'Who visited?' triggers the same speech bubble with 'Thanks!' button and adds the 'Roy (Beau) — Butler IM' panel in the right sidebar listing the recent visitors.
difference: None — behavior, popup menu options, speech bubble dialog, and sidebar Butler IM match the original.

original_shows: Clicking the Magic Rock opens a menu with 'House keys', 'Customize', 'Change style', 'Expand', and 'Cultivate land'. Selecting 'Change style' opens a modal with 6 street style thumbnails (including Forgotten Growth, Floral Tangles, Vorn Road). Selecting Vorn Road opens a preview banner with 'Cancel' and 'Change to this', then a confirmation prompt ('Are you sure you want to change your street style for 190i? Nevermind / Yes, change it'), deducts 190 iMG, shows a loading screen ('Changing street style / Sit tight, it'll be ready shortly! / reticulating splines...'), and reloads the Home Street with the snowy Vorn Road background.
rebuild_shows: Clicking the Magic Rock opens a menu with 'House keys', 'Customize', 'Change style', 'Expand', and 'Cultivate land'. Selecting 'Change style' opens a modal with the 6 street style options, previews Vorn Road with 'Cancel' / 'Change to this' and the 190i confirmation ('Nevermind' / 'Yes, change it'), deducts 190 iMG, shows the 'Changing street style / Sit tight, it'll be ready shortly!' loading screen with 'reticulating splines...', and updates the street background to snowy Vorn Road.
difference: None significant; the menu options, modal flow, 190 iMG cost, loading screen, and resulting snowy Vorn Road theme all match.

original_shows: On Bongul Beat, clicking the stationary 'Street Spirit (Animal Goods Vendor)' NPC opens an 'Animal Goods Vendor' popup window with 'Buy' and 'Sell' tabs, displaying items on a shelf with their currant prices and the player's current balance ('You have 1,461 currants').
rebuild_shows: On Bongul Beat, interacting with the stationary Street Spirit NPC opens the 'Street Spirit (Animal Goods Vendor)' modal with 'Buy' and 'Sell' tabs, item cards with currant prices, and the player's currant balance. The player purchases 'Butterfly Lotion' for 45 currants, deducting from their currant total.
difference: None regarding the rule under test (UI layout uses a grid of item cards instead of a single shelf row, which is an acceptable stylistic adaptation).

original_shows: On Bongul Beat, the player encounters a wandering Chicken, clicks on it to squeeze it, and receives '+1 mood' floating text while holding/squeezing it, and also sees a butterfly flying nearby.
rebuild_shows: On Bongul Beat in Andra, there is a Chicken, a Piggy, and a Butterfly. The player squeezes the Chicken for '+1 mood' floating text, and pets the Piggy for 'Oink! +4 mood +5 iMG' floating text.
difference: None for the rule under test (art is simplified, and the player doesn't physically walk over to pick up the chicken before squeezing, though the action menu and +1 mood feedback match).

original_shows: Cubimals (such as Dustbunny Cubimal Lvl 1 and Firebog Street Spirit Cubimal) race along the ground and log the distance traveled in planks (e.g., 'stormoffaire's Dustbunny Cubimal Lvl 1 went 2.33 planks before stopping.') in both a bottom-screen notification and the Local Chat / Activity log.
rebuild_shows: Beau sets out 'Chick Cubimal Lv1.1', which appears on the ground with a floating distance label, accompanied by the bottom notification and Local Chat log: 'Beau's Chick Cubimal Lv1.1 went 3.40 planks before stopping.'
difference: None significant; the Cubimal racing mechanic and plank-distance reporting match the original.

original_shows: Inside Andra Bureaucratic Hall, frog-like Bureaucrat NPCs (Director Wigglesbottom, Secretary Wigglesbottom, Magister Piksnikson) sit at desks and cubicles. The player clicks Director Wigglesbottom, who shows a speech bubble instructing the player to wait, followed by a bottom dialog prompt 'Please move into the waiting area to your left.' Once the player walks into the waiting area, a 'Please Wait' progress bar appears at the top right, and trying to move triggers a bottom prompt 'You can't do anything while waiting. Just wait.'
rebuild_shows: The rebuild has simple green blob characters with no desks, cubicles, or speech bubbles. The waiting timer is a text box ('Please Wait — Do not move, just wait, all true. 15 secs') instead of the progress bar UI, and dialogue only appears in the right-hand chat log rather than in-world speech bubbles and bottom modal prompts.
difference: Missing in-world speech bubbles, bottom modal prompts ('Please move into the waiting area to your left' / 'You can't do anything while waiting. Just wait.'), the 'Please Wait' progress bar UI at top right, and the desk/cubicle office environment and frog NPC sprites.
fix_hint: Add speech bubbles for the bureaucrat NPCs, the bottom-right 'Ok' modal prompts when initiating waiting or attempting to move while waiting, the top-right 'Please Wait' progress bar widget, and proper desk/cubicle visuals for the bureaucrats.

original_shows: When a Giant appears (e.g., Cosma), the game viewport dims with a dark overlay, the large intricate Giant totem/visage floats in on the left side of the viewport (above the character), and to the right of the visage a large header 'Cosma says...' with multi-line announcement text and a 'Click anywhere...' prompt at the bottom appears.
rebuild_shows: A shrine on the street where the player clicks 'Donate to Grendaline (+Favor)' and receives '+10 Favor with Grendaline! +20 iMG'. Then a Giant visage ('Alph says...') appears centered in the screen with a simplistic sun-like SVG icon stacked vertically above the text 'Alph says...' and announcement text.
difference: In the original, the Giant visage and announcement text are arranged side-by-side (visage on the left, 'Cosma says...' and paragraph text on the right, left-aligned) with a 'Click anywhere...' indicator below the text. In the rebuild, the visage and text are stacked vertically and centered in the middle of the screen. Also the Giant artwork is an overly simple geometric shape rather than an ornate totem visage.
fix_hint: Change the Giant visage overlay layout from a centered vertical column to a horizontal side-by-side layout: position the large ornate Giant totem artwork on the left half of the viewport (floating/bobbing gently) and the '<Giant> says...' heading + paragraph text + 'Click anywhere...' prompt in a left-aligned column to its right.

original_shows: On Beau's Home Street, the player walks past two Wood Trees (wooden post/log-like trees with plank branches) and a construction project. When hovering over a Wood Tree or project, a blue selection outline appears. (Earlier clips in the game show clicking a tree opens a radial/pie menu with interaction options like Water, Pet, Harvest, followed by an interaction animation and floating harvest feedback).
rebuild_shows: On Beau's Home Street, there are two Wood Trees. Without walking up to the tree or opening an interaction menu, floating text 'Watered! +4 iMG +2 mood' and 'Harvested 2x Plank +5 iMG' simultaneously pops up over the tree from a distance, and a full-screen 'Alph says...' modal immediately covers the screen.
difference:
1. There is no radial/pie action menu shown when clicking the Wood Tree to choose Water, Pet, or Harvest.
2. The player does not walk over to the tree or play watering/harvesting animations.
3. Both watering and harvesting happen instantaneously from afar with simple floating text instead of proper sequential interaction feedback.
4. The background and lighting of Beau's Home Street (bright snowy pines in rebuild vs dark spooky forest in original) and the tree art differ, though art differences are secondary to the missing interaction menu and animations.
fix_hint: Implement the radial interaction menu (Water, Pet, Harvest) when clicking on a Wood Tree, require the player to walk to the tree before performing the action, and display the watering/harvesting progress/animations rather than triggering instant remote actions.
test_problem: The automated test triggers water and harvest actions directly/instantly in the same tick and leaves an 'Alph says...' modal open over the screen.

original_shows: Beau clicks the Beryl Rock, selects 'Help mine' while DeadSparrow is already mining it. A green 'mine' progress bar fills over several seconds while both players show pickaxe thought bubbles. Upon completion, it yields -7 Energy, +10 iMG, +8 Chunks of Beryl, and a +1 bonus chunk ('You got 1 additional Chunk of Beryl with the help you received from DeadSparrow').
rebuild_shows: In the second player's clip, mining the Beryl Rock completes instantaneously ('You mined a Beryl Rock. -7 Energy +10 iMG +8 Chunks of Beryl') and also erroneously triggers an 'Alph says...' giant shrine overlay modal. Because mining is instant and has no progress bar duration, the first player cannot join in to co-mine (and their test step times out).
difference: 1. Mining is instantaneous instead of taking several seconds with a green 'mine' progress bar and pickaxe thought bubbles, preventing simultaneous co-mining and the +1 bonus chunk. 2. Clicking/mining the Beryl Rock triggers an unrelated 'Alph says...' modal.
fix_hint: Add a timed mining channel/progress bar ('mine') with pickaxe thought bubbles when mining rocks so a second player can click 'Help mine' during the channel to trigger the co-op +1 bonus chunk. Also fix click/interaction handling so mining a rock does not trigger the Alph shrine dialog.
test_problem: Step 7 timed out because player 2's mining completed instantly instead of staying in a mining state for player 1 to 'Help mine', and an Alph modal blocked the screen.

original_shows: In Bongul Beat, the brown Dirt Pile is on the ground level (to the left of the tree). Clicking it shows 'Dirt Pile' with 'Dig (requires working shovel)'.
rebuild_shows: In Bongul Beat, the Dirt Pile is placed on a floating wooden platform above the ground. Clicking it shows 'Dirt Pile' with 'Dig (-5e)', and digging it yields '+2 Lumps of Earth +7 iMG' (with 'Your bag is full!' warning).
difference: 1. The Dirt Pile in Bongul Beat is on an elevated floating platform in the rebuild instead of on the ground level as in the original. 2. In the original, digging is a channeled/progress-bar action with a shovel animation (as seen at B 03:01), whereas in the rebuild clicking 'Dig (-5e)' instantly harvests it without a shovel animation or progress bar.
fix_hint: Place the Dirt Pile on the ground level in Bongul Beat (not on a floating platform) and add a digging progress bar / shovel animation when digging.
test_problem: The player's inventory is full during the test ('Your bag is full! Drop or consume an item first.'), so the Lumps of Earth aren't actually added to the inventory slots.

original_shows: Floating circular orbs (Quoins) with icons inside (blue mood icon, yellow currant icon, green energy icon, purple xp icon) hover in the air. When the player jumps through them, they expand/pop into large circular rings and white floating text ('+1 mood', '+1 currants', '+1 xp', '+1 energy') drifts upward.
rebuild_shows: Floating circular orbs hover in the air on Bongul Beat. When the player jumps through them, they disappear and colored floating text ('+1 mood', '+1 currants') appears, though the text is colored green/yellow instead of white and lacks the expanding ring pop animation.
difference: In the original, collecting a Quoin triggers an expanding white circular ring animation and displays white floating text with a dark outline/shadow ('+1 mood', '+1 currants', etc.). In the rebuild, there is no expanding ring pop animation and the floating reward text is colored (green for mood, yellow for currants) and much smaller/harder to read.
fix_hint: Add the expanding ring pop effect when Quoins are collected, and style the floating reward text ('+1 mood', '+1 currants', '+1 xp', '+1 energy') in larger bold white font with a subtle shadow/outline as seen in the original.

original_shows: In the original clip, the bottom bar has 16 primary slots (containing bags with slot counts like 16/16 beneath them), an expanded row of 16 sub-slots directly above the primary slots when a bag is selected, 'Inventory' and 'Furniture' mode tabs on the left above the sub-slots, and a magnifying glass icon next to those tabs that opens a popup 'Search inventory for:' text box directly above the tabs.
rebuild_shows: The rebuild has 16 primary slots at the bottom, 'Inventory' and 'Furniture' tabs on the left, and when 'Generic Green Bag' is opened, a row of sub-slots appears above the tabs. However, the search bar ('Search inventory for:') is permanently visible on the far right side rather than being a toggleable magnifying glass icon next to the Inventory/Furniture tabs on the left, and the bag slots lack the capacity indicators (e.g. '5/6' or '16/16') below them.
difference: 1. The search filter in the original is a magnifying glass icon on the left side (next to the Inventory/Furniture tabs) that toggles a popup input box above it, whereas the rebuild places a permanent search input box on the far right. 2. In the original, the expanded bag sub-slots appear directly between the primary slots and the Inventory/Furniture tabs (pushing the tabs up), whereas in the rebuild the expanded bag row appears above the Inventory/Furniture tabs. 3. Primary bag slots in the original show capacity bars/numbers (e.g. '16/16', '5/16') underneath each slot, which are missing in the rebuild.
fix_hint: Move the search filter to a magnifying glass toggle button on the left next to the 'Inventory' and 'Furniture' tabs, make the expanded bag sub-slot row appear directly above the 16 primary slots (with the tabs and search button sitting above the sub-slot row), and add slot usage/capacity labels underneath bag slots in the primary bar.

original_shows: Clicking '12-sided Die' in the inventory opens a white rounded popup above the slot with the item title ('12-sided Die'), subtitle/description ('But there are only 11 sides.'), and action links: 'Give', 'Drop', 'Roll', plus a small '(i)' inspect icon in the top-right corner of the popup.
rebuild_shows: Clicking '12-sided Die' in the inventory opens a context menu with '12-sided Die (1)', 'Roll', 'Inspect', 'Drop'. It is missing the item description subtitle and the 'Give' option (and 'Inspect' is a text list item rather than an icon).
difference: The inventory item context menu in the rebuild lacks the 'Give' action and the item's flavour text subtitle ('But there are only 11 sides.'), and renders 'Inspect' as a menu row instead of an info icon.
fix_hint: Add the 'Give' option to inventory item context menus, display the item's subtitle/description under the title in the popup, and use an info icon for Inspect.

original_shows: When clicking the Water Cooler with a full inventory, the interaction popup directly shows 'Your bag is full!' above a disabled/greyed-out 'Get water' button. To free up a slot, the player clicks an item in the inventory bar to open its action menu and consumes or drops it.
rebuild_shows: Clicking the Water Cooler shows an active 'Get water (-2e)' button; clicking it displays a floating red 'Your bag is full!' text and a chat message. Then, when the test tries to drop a 12-sided Die (stack of 16) from the last slot, dropping only reduces the stack from 16 to 15 rather than freeing the slot, so the second attempt to get water also fails with 'Your bag is full!'.
difference: 1) In the original, 'Your bag is full!' is shown inside the Water Cooler's interaction menu with the button disabled when the bag is full, whereas the rebuild allows clicking 'Get water' and shows floating error text. 2) Dropping a stacked item in the rebuild only drops 1 from the stack (16 -> 15) instead of dropping the stack or freeing the slot, preventing the test from freeing a slot to test acquiring the Cup of Water.
fix_hint: Disable the 'Get water' button and show 'Your bag is full!' inside the interaction menu when the inventory has no free slots. Also check whether 'Drop' on a stack should drop the whole stack (or have the test put a single non-stacked item in the 16th slot so dropping it frees the slot).
test_problem: The test filled the 16th inventory slot with a stack of 16 12-sided Dice; clicking 'Drop' once only decremented the stack to 15, leaving all 16 slots occupied so the Cup of Water could never be acquired.

original_shows: In the original clip, the top-left HUD shows 'iMG 26,036' (which decreases by 190 when changing street style). Across the full original footage referenced in the rule, Currants are shown in the HUD/profile and Credits are shown in the wardrobe.
rebuild_shows: The top HUD clearly displays 'iMG 25,190' and '1,441 c' (Currants with a gold coin icon). When the Wardrobe modal opens at 00:02-00:03, it clearly displays '2,748 Credits' in the top right of the modal and prices items in credits.
difference: None regarding the presence and display of the three currencies.
test_problem: The automated assertion failed (`ok: false`), even though the rebuild visually displays all three currencies (iMG and Currants in the top HUD, Credits in the Wardrobe modal) as expected by the test description. Check the DOM selectors used in the test assertion.

original_shows: In the top-left HUD, the circular Mood gauge and blue Energy bar are overlaid inside the main game canvas at the top-left corner, while the player avatar, name, and iMG counter sit in the white header bar above the canvas.
rebuild_shows: In the rebuild, the circular Mood gauge and Energy bar are placed inside the white top header bar, and the player avatar/name are missing from the top-left corner.
difference: The layout of the top-left HUD differs: the original places the circular Mood gauge and Energy bar as an overlay inside the top-left corner of the viewport canvas (below the header bar containing the avatar, name, and iMG), whereas the rebuild puts all of them inline in the top header bar and omits the avatar/name.
fix_hint: Move the circular Mood gauge and Energy bar overlay into the top-left corner of the game viewport canvas, and place the player avatar, name ('Beau'), and iMG counter in the top header bar above it.

original_shows: A full-page Skills encyclopedia UI featuring a periodic-table-like grid of all skills at the bottom (grouped by Animals, Growing, Gathering, Cooking, Alchemy, Intellectual, Industrial with a color legend for Learned, Learnable, Not learnable yet, Learning, Required), a category sidebar on the left (All Learnable, Alchemy, Animals, Cooking, Gathering, Growing, Industrial, Intellectual) with detailed skill cards on the right, a Brain Capacity bar in the top right (101+1 / 33 Skills, 2764% time penalty), and clicking a skill opens a detailed modal showing the real-time duration (e.g. '4 days 3 hr 6 min 12 sec'), description, Requirements (Level, prior skills, upgrades), Giant affiliation, and Status.
rebuild_shows: A simplified 'Skills & Quest Log' popup modal inside the game canvas showing a 2x4 grid of basic skill cards with 'Learn (time)' buttons, a static text line for Brain Capacity and Currently Learning at the top, and an Active Quest Log at the bottom. Clicking a button simply switches the active learning skill without showing prerequisites, skill tree grid, or category filtering.
difference: The rebuild completely omits the iconic periodic-table skill tree visualization, category sidebar filtering, and the detailed skill inspection modal showing prerequisites (level, prior skills, upgrades) and giant affiliations. It replaces the entire skills UI with a basic 8-card popup combined with the quest log.
fix_hint: Implement the full Skills UI layout: include the category tabs/sidebar (All Learnable, Alchemy, Animals, etc.), the periodic-table-style skill tree grid with legend, the Brain Capacity progress bar header, and the skill detail modal displaying prerequisites (Level, prior skills, quests/upgrades) and giant affiliation when clicking a skill.

original_shows: Clicking 'Spend' on an 'Emblem of Friendly' opens a 'Please Confirm!' modal dialog asking 'Are you sure you want to spend this Emblem of Friendly to reduce the learning time of [Skill] by [Time]? Note! Friendly is not affiliated with this skill, so spending their Emblem won't speed up learning as much.' with Yes/No buttons. Clicking 'Contemplate' awards +36 iMG (with a floating '+36 iMG' near the top-left iMG counter and chat message 'You Contemplated an Emblem of Friendly (+36 iMG)').
rebuild_shows: Spending the Emblem of Friendly immediately consumes it without any confirmation dialog, shows floating text 'You spended an Emblem! +34 iMG' above the player avatar, and logs 'You spended an Emblem of Friendly! +34 iMG & skill learning sped up!' in chat.
difference: 1) The original shows a 'Please Confirm!' modal dialog when clicking 'Spend' on an Emblem to reduce skill learning time, whereas the rebuild skips the confirmation dialog entirely. 2) The original separates 'Spend' (reduces skill learning time with confirmation) and 'Contemplate' (awards iMG), whereas the rebuild combines them into 'Spend' and uses ungrammatical text ('You spended an Emblem!'). 3) In the rebuild clip, the inventory slot for the Emblem isn't even visible (empty slots at the bottom) and no context menu interaction is shown.
fix_hint: Add the 'Please Confirm!' modal when spending an Emblem to reduce skill learning time, separate 'Spend' (learning time reduction) from 'Contemplate' (+iMG), and fix the message grammar ('spended' -> 'spent' / 'Contemplated'). Also ensure emblems in inventory render their icons and context menus.
test_problem: The test appears to trigger the item use programmatically without opening the inventory item context menu or showing the Emblem item in the inventory bar.

original_shows: Clicking 'Quest Log' opens a dedicated Quest Log modal window where each quest has a green/yellow title, description with underlined clickable links for items/locations (e.g., 'Watering Can', 'Shovel', 'Lumps of Earth'), visual icon-based progress counters below the text (e.g., watering can icon with '4/5') that show hover tooltips (e.g., 'Water trees'), 'Try it' buttons, and a right-aligned reward summary line.
rebuild_shows: Clicking 'Skills & Quests' opens a combined modal showing the skills tree on top and a plain text list of quests at the bottom. The quests lack clickable item/location links, lack visual step-by-step objective icon counters with tooltips, and merely show plain text like 'Give some H2O love (5/5)' and 'COMPLETED'.
difference: The Quest Log in the rebuild is merged into the Skills modal instead of being a dedicated view (or properly styled section), and it completely lacks clickable underlined item/location links, step-by-step objective icons with counters and hover tooltips, and 'Try it' / hint buttons.
